replies.tweet_text: I think most people dont really understand what opec is and why the UAE leaving it does not matter much. OPEC is a price setting cartel. Their true function is to control supplies among members through quotas so their is a mutually beneficial average price for all. Gulf
replies.reply_text: My read: right about the mechanism, wrong about the consequence. ADNOC's current capacity is 4.8M bpd against an OPEC ceiling of 3.4M, and that 1.4M bpd overhang is now free. The real story is whether Saudi Arabia defends price floor or market share when UAE floods supply.
replies.reply_angle: counters 'doesn't matter' argument with production math, reframes as Saudi forced-choice story between price floor and volume

replies.tweet_text: REACTION COLUMN: Why is the UAE leaving OPEC? The announcement has little to do with the US-Iran war; the exit road started in Riyadh, with a detour in Texas. It's all about the UAE wanting to pump more oil, even at the cost of lower prices.
replies.reply_text: My read: the production case was always there, 4.8M capacity vs 3.4M quota for years. The Iran war didn't create the motive, it removed the diplomatic cost of acting on it. OPEC members do not attack each other's refineries in peacetime.
replies.reply_angle: extends Blas's production argument while adding the diplomatic-cost mechanism explaining why the war was catalytic, not coincidental
